articles.title: Dewford won the possessions that needed finishing
articles.dek: Mauville gained more yards. The Breakers returned a kickoff ninety-nine yards, won third down and secured a playoff berth. Brawly should preserve those strengths while asking more of the offense.
articles.author: mara-voss

body.text: Dewford’s 21–13 win over Mauville belongs first to Meowscarada’s ninety-nine-yard kickoff return and a defense that stopped all eight of the Dynamos’ third-down attempts. I want those contributions named before anyone waves the total-yardage comparison around as an explanation of the game. Mauville gained 280 yards to Dewford’s 194. The Breakers scored the return touchdown, completed the useful short scoring passes and made the opponent repeatedly start over.

That is a specific way to win, and Brawly now has ten victories and a playoff berth. It also asks a sensible question of the offense before the trip to Rustboro: how much of this can it reproduce when the kickoff does not immediately become seven points? I like Dewford’s discipline on the decisive downs. I want more dependable rushing production to accompany it. Both judgments follow from the same afternoon.

Frosmoth completed eleven of fifteen passes for 129 yards and two touchdowns. He also threw an interception on the opening possession. The four incompletions include a meaningful mistake, not just harmless attempts that failed to connect. Mauville converted the interception into a field goal. Dewford then responded with a thirteen-yard short-left touchdown to Boldore and began to put the game back on its own terms.
The return changed the next assignment

Mauville moved ahead 10–7 on Togekiss’s eight-yard touchdown pass to Vanillish early in the second quarter. The advantage lasted through the extra point and no longer. Meowscarada returned the ensuing kickoff ninety-nine yards for a touchdown, immediately restoring Dewford’s lead. The Breakers did not need to drive the length of the field to answer the score because their return unit had completed that work in one play.

The sequence matters tactically. Mauville’s offense had just done enough to score, yet its next possession would again begin with a deficit to overcome. Dewford’s offense received the benefit of a lead without having to expose itself to another series of downs. Special teams supplied points and changed the pressure on the following possessions. Treating that as background noise to the passing totals would miss the central event.

Frosmoth added a nine-yard short-left touchdown to Swellow at 1:41 of the second quarter. Dewford led 21–10 at halftime and scored no more. The defense then had to protect the advantage through the entire second half. It did, with help from a recovered fumble and an interception, but the scoreless offensive half should be part of Brawly’s preparation for Rustboro rather than politely removed from it.
Third down is a repeatable assignment

The Breakers went four for eight on third down while Mauville went zero for eight. That comparison gives me more confidence in their process than the final margin alone. Dewford extended half of its third-down possessions; the Dynamos extended none. An offense can gain two hundred forty-seven passing yards and still fail to maintain enough series if those gains do not arrive when another first down is required.

Togekiss completed nineteen of twenty-nine for those 247 yards. Tangrowth caught eighty-three and Arbok seventy-nine. Mauville had useful receivers making useful gains. The problem was the next necessary conversion and the possessions lost to mistakes. Wugtrio fumbled after a seven-yard reception in the third quarter, with Carnivine recovering. Thievul intercepted a deep-right pass in the fourth. Dewford’s defense converted pressure on the result into actual possession changes.

The rushing comparison is less flattering to either offense. Dewford ran twenty-nine times for sixty-five yards, while Mauville managed thirty-three on eleven carries. Excadrill gained forty-six on eighteen attempts. Those numbers do not establish a ground game that can reliably decide a playoff possession by itself. The Breakers need to identify which rushing assignments create useful next downs and which merely consume one of the three available chances.

Frosmoth took no sacks. That is another practical strength to retain. A quarterback who attempts only fifteen passes cannot afford to surrender several of the limited passing opportunities before releasing the ball. Dewford kept those attempts available, completed eleven and turned two into touchdowns. The task is to preserve that efficiency while improving the rest of the possession, rather than demanding a larger passing total for its own sake.
Rustboro provides a useful final test

The Stone have just allowed Petalburg to win with two touchdown passes and no turnovers. Rustboro also forced six punts and limited the Pride to two successful third downs in ten attempts. Dewford should expect the next game to require patient finishing. A ninety-nine-yard return is welcome; it is a poor assumption to build into the next offensive plan.

A Breakers win or tie keeps fifth seed. A loss gives fifth to Rustboro and moves Dewford to sixth. The berth is already secured, so Brawly can assess the final game through both seeding and preparation. Neither purpose requires pretending the offense was flawless against Mauville. Nine first downs and a scoreless second half leave clear room for improvement even in a victory worth celebrating.

I would keep the protection standard, demand the same concentration on third down and examine every rushing call that left Frosmoth with an unnecessarily difficult next attempt. The defense has supplied a playoff berth. The return unit supplied seven points that Mauville could not recover. Dewford’s offense now has one regular-season game to make its own contribution more dependable before every possession can end the season.

articles.title: Cianwood has one more meaningful week
articles.dek: Bibarel’s 106 rushing yards and Gurdurr’s late takeaways kept the Crushers alive. A trip to Mt. Silver now carries a difficult but definite playoff route.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Cianwood completed three passes at Olivine and won the game. I keep returning to that combination because it contains both the limitation of the Crushers’ afternoon and the reason their final week still matters. They beat the Ironclads 10–3, improved to 7–9 and retained a route to the playoffs. It is a demanding route, beginning with a victory at Mt. Silver, but the team has earned the right to prepare for it.

Bibarel ran twenty-nine times for 106 yards. Gurdurr recovered a fourth-quarter fumble and intercepted a pass later in the same period. Charjabug made a fifty-five-yard field goal. Crobat caught the fifty-yard touchdown that supplied the game’s only trip to the end zone. A small number of contributors did very specific work, and Cianwood’s defense made that work sufficient.

The passing line remains difficult to admire without qualification. Swampert completed three of twelve attempts for sixty-five yards, one touchdown and one interception. The Crushers also lost a fumble. They did not produce a complete offensive performance simply because the opponent scored three. Their achievement was to keep playing usefully around the limitations until Olivine ran out of opportunities.
Bibarel kept accepting the next carry

There is a quieter form of persistence in twenty-nine carries. Bibarel’s 106 yards came at a little under four per attempt. Cianwood did not have an effortless offense in which every run opened a large space. It had a runner repeatedly taking the next assignment while the passing game struggled to complete ordinary work. Those carries helped the Crushers finish with 131 rushing yards as a team.

Cianwood converted four of eleven third downs. That is useful beside Olivine’s one conversion in ten attempts, although it still leaves seven third downs the Crushers did not convert. The difference gave their offense enough chances to protect a narrow lead. It also helps explain why the defense’s late interventions were necessary rather than decorative additions to an already comfortable victory.

Crobat’s touchdown came at 3:46 of the second quarter on a deep-right pass from Swampert. The fifty-yard reception accounted for most of the quarterback’s passing yardage. Crobat finished with two catches for fifty-six yards, leaving one other completion for nine. One large play made the offense productive enough to win; it did not make the broader completion problem disappear.

I am reluctant to turn that into a sermon about how a team ought to win. Cianwood used what worked. The defense repeatedly prevented Olivine from doing the same. The useful question for the next week is how the Crushers can retain the dependable parts of this performance while asking less of a single long touchdown. Against a fourteen-win opponent, three completions would leave very little room for error.
Gurdurr gave the lead two more chances to survive

The fourth quarter presented Cianwood with exactly the kind of mistake a narrow lead cannot comfortably absorb. Doduo fumbled after a six-yard run up the middle at 4:22, and Octillery recovered for Olivine. The Ironclads had another opportunity to erase the seven-point deficit. Cianwood’s defense answered before that opportunity could become points.

At 3:42, Drampa completed a sixteen-yard short-left pass to Gastrodon, who fumbled. Gurdurr recovered. Later, with 1:46 remaining, Gurdurr intercepted Drampa’s short-left throw and returned it twelve yards. Those plays gave the Crushers relief at moments when their own offense had not created enough separation to tolerate an opposing touchdown.

Olivine took five sacks for thirty-two lost yards, punted seven times and finished with five first downs. The defense had made a seven-point lead workable by repeatedly removing the opponent’s ability to sustain a drive. Cianwood’s offensive problems remain part of the evaluation, but the defensive work deserves to be described as a performance in its own right.
A recovered designation creates a question, not an answer

Gardevoir’s remaining injury absence has reached zero before the finale. That is a relevant change at quarterback after Swampert’s difficult passing afternoon. It does not announce a starter, confirm an activation or establish how the next game’s snaps will be divided. Cianwood can prepare with more information than it had last week, while the actual assignment remains to be made.

Haunter continues with two reported weeks out. The receiver’s absence is another reason to keep the passing discussion specific. The Crushers need completions from the players who can take the field. A recovered quarterback designation and one successful deep throw are promising pieces of information, but neither provides an entire receiving plan for Mt. Silver.

The playoff route is exact. Cianwood must beat the Reds, Olivine must lose at Azalea, Violet must lose to Mahogany, and Cerulean must fail to beat Vermilion. That combination gives the Crushers the final berth. Other combinations eliminate them. The route is a statement of what would be required, rather than an estimate of how likely those results are.

Mt. Silver has secured the first seed and bye, but that does not establish which players it will use or how difficult the game will be. The Reds just produced 453 yards in a 41–9 win. Cianwood must prepare for the quality it has observed, then adjust to the lineup that actually appears. Hoping for an opponent’s generosity is a poor substitute for a useful first possession.

The Crushers have given themselves one more week in which preparation can change their season’s ending. Bibarel has twenty-nine carries to recover from and another assignment to prepare for. The defense has a strong performance to repeat. The passing game has clear work to improve. For a 7–9 team with a difficult route, those are meaningful things to have waiting on the next practice field.

articles.title: Blaine has another receiver ready for the argument
articles.dek: Glalie caught twelve passes for 154 yards and two touchdowns at Celadon. Cinnabar’s fourth seed comes with a passing game its first-round visitor must take seriously.
articles.author: dorian-pike

body.text: Blaine, keep throwing to Glalie. There is my recommendation, delivered early enough that nobody can accuse me of hiding it behind the playoff bracket. Twelve catches, 154 yards and two touchdowns in a 24–7 win at Celadon constitute a rather persuasive application for more work. Cinnabar is 11–5, the fourth seed is secured, and the Blaze have found another substantial receiving contribution before their first home playoff game.

I have been accused of liking Cinnabar too much. The recent schedule has been unusually considerate of my position. The Blaze beat Blackthorn, beat Mt. Silver and then beat Celadon. The first two victories established their ability to trouble leading teams; the third showed that they could carry productive passing into the next assignment while the backfield was dealing with injuries.

Gholdengo completed twenty-three of thirty-five passes for 296 yards and three touchdowns. He took no sacks. Glalie supplied more than half of the passing yardage, while Exploud contributed forty-eight rushing yards and thirty-nine receiving yards. Cinnabar had enough different work around the lead receiver to finish with 358 total yards and seventeen first downs. This was an offense with a productive central connection and several supporting contributions.
Twelve catches create a recurring obligation for the defense

A receiver who catches one long touchdown can make a defense regret one snap. Twelve receptions create a much longer meeting. Glalie’s first score came on an eight-yard deep-left throw at 1:29 of the opening quarter. The second came on a twelve-yard short-left completion in the third. The two touchdowns used different passing descriptions and arrived on opposite sides of halftime.

That matters because the receiving line was not built around a single forty- or fifty-yard play that dwarfed everything else. Glalie kept appearing in completed passes. Gholdengo had a target who could contribute repeatedly while the offense moved through the game’s ordinary downs. A playoff opponent must account for that repeated usefulness as well as the two scoring moments.

Celadon tied the game at seven late in the second quarter on Infernape’s two-yard touchdown to Carnivine. Cinnabar answered with Charjabug’s twenty-six-yard field goal before halftime, then scored two touchdowns in the third. The Blaze did not require an immediate rout to maintain control. They accepted a close game, continued the passing work and produced the separation after the break.

Buizel caught the other touchdown, a five-yard short-left pass at 1:19 of the third. That score is a useful reminder that a defense cannot simply send every available concern toward Glalie. The Blaze’s quarterback still has to recognize where the completion belongs. Gholdengo found three touchdown throws and only one interception, giving the offense enough successful decisions to carry the afternoon.
Protection allowed the receivers to matter

No sacks on thirty-five pass attempts is a practical achievement. The protection did not automatically complete the throws, and Celadon recorded nine pass breakups, so the passing game still had to solve coverage. It did prevent the offense from repeatedly losing yards before those coverage questions could be answered. Cinnabar’s receivers had opportunities to do the work their production now advertises.

The Blaze converted five of nine third downs. Celadon went four for ten and punted five times. Those differences were not overwhelming in isolation, but they supported the larger pattern: Cinnabar sustained more useful possessions and finished three with passing touchdowns. The Bloom finished with one. The seventeen-point margin came from that accumulated work, not from a defensive score or a return touchdown.

Gholdengo’s fourth-quarter interception also belongs in the account. Ampharos picked a short-right attempt with 5:41 remaining. Cinnabar’s defense prevented Celadon from turning the mistake into a scoring recovery. The win does not justify removing the error; it gives Blaine a specific late-game decision to address before a playoff opponent can make the next one more expensive.
The backfield remains a current problem

Arcanine is still out two reported weeks. Seismitoad’s remaining absence has reached zero, which provides a relevant availability change without announcing the next starting role. Exploud’s forty-eight rushing yards at Celadon demonstrate that the Blaze found useful work from an available runner. They do not prove that every missing part of the backfield has been replaced.

Cinnabar gained sixty-two rushing yards on nineteen attempts as a team. That total leaves room for an opponent to make the offense more dependent on passing. A defense that can reduce Glalie’s repeated completions while keeping the rushing game near that level would present a harder assignment than the Blaze faced in their most successful stretches here. My confidence in Cinnabar should survive an honest description of the remaining challenge.

The finale is at Pewter. The Rockers just came back to beat Viridian 20–13, so their recent result offers more resistance than a glance at the six-win record might suggest. Cinnabar’s fourth seed is fixed, but the final regular-season game still provides an opportunity to organize the available backfield and maintain the passing connection that has made these last three wins so useful.
Cinnabar knows the two possible visitors

Blackthorn and Lavender will settle Johto East in their head-to-head finale. The club that does not win the division finishes fifth and travels to Cinnabar. A Lavender victory sends Blackthorn to the Blaze; a Blackthorn win or tie sends Lavender. That gives Blaine two concrete opponents to study without pretending the final result has already been decided.

Blackthorn has a fresh two-week absence for Exploud and has just recovered from its Saffron defeat with a win at Mahogany. Lavender has a quarterback coming off five touchdown passes and a defense coming off four interceptions. Either visitor will bring a meaningful challenge. Neither has been granted permission to treat the fourth seed as a comfortable destination merely because its number is larger than three.

Glalie’s twelve catches give Cinnabar a current, specific receiving argument. Gholdengo’s protection and distribution give that argument support. The defense held Celadon to seven points, and the team has now won eleven games. Blaine’s next responsibility is to preserve those useful parts, repair the remaining backfield questions and make whichever fifth seed arrives spend the afternoon answering the same difficult passing assignments.

articles.title: Injury Report: playoff offenses lose Holt, Gyarzalez, Oinkologne and Tatsugiri
articles.dek: The final-round availability report covers new absences, recovery countdowns and cleared remaining weeks across the league.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: The final regular-season week arrives with new absences for several playoff clubs. Mossdeep’s Poury Holt is out seven reported weeks, Mt. Silver’s Tony Gyarzalez six, Petalburg’s Oinkologne three and Eterna quarterback Tatsugiri seven. Canalave, still pursuing the last wild card, has lost Nidoking for nine weeks and Seismitoad for six. These are current reported durations, not confirmed return dates.
Contenders must replace productive work

Holt ran for 115 yards in Mossdeep’s 22–3 win and caught a five-yard pass. The Eclipse have already secured the first seed and bye, but that protection in the bracket does not supply his rushing production. Shawn Mareman contributed forty-eight yards on eight carries in the same game, an observed alternative contribution rather than an announced future assignment. Richard Furman’s remaining absence has reached zero, although his injured-reserve status still requires a separate roster decision.

Gyarzalez caught five passes for fifty-six yards while Crem Ftzpatrik threw for 318 in Mt. Silver’s win at Azalea. The Reds also have a new two-week absence for Ninjask. Their bye is secured, allowing preparation time after the finale, but neither duration establishes who will be available in a particular playoff game. Foo Warner’s remaining absence has reached zero.

Petalburg secured Hoenn West while Oinkologne generated eighty-nine rushing yards on five carries and thirty receiving yards. His three-week designation removes a substantial part of the offense that beat Rustboro. Whiscash had twelve carries for minus-two yards in that game. Seviper’s previous one-week absence has reached zero, providing a useful receiving-status change while leaving the future lineup unconfirmed.

Eterna’s new seven-week designation for Tatsugiri changes the preparation for a division champion. Stantler is also out two weeks. The Thorns have won with a low-scoring profile and a defense that has allowed 181 points through sixteen games; the available offense must now be reassessed for Snowpoint and the coming home playoff game. No replacement start is announced by this report.
The last-berth races have changed personnel

Canalave beat Snowpoint 24–21 with sixty rushing yards from Nidoking, who now has a nine-week absence. Seismitoad is out six weeks. Delcatty contributed forty-five rushing yards in the win, but that does not establish a complete replacement plan for the trip to Oreburgh. Canalave must win and receive help from Mauville’s result to guarantee the final berth.

Olivine’s Gogoat is out five weeks after the 10–3 loss to Cianwood. Bibarel’s remaining absence has reached zero. The Ironclads still qualify by beating Azalea, so the backfield changes arrive before a game they can use to settle the race themselves. Violet’s Zangoose, who ran for fifty-one yards against Lavender, is out four weeks before the Falcons host Mahogany.

Cianwood’s Gardevoir has reached zero remaining weeks. That is a meaningful quarterback availability update after Swampert completed three of twelve passes in the win over Olivine. It does not confirm Gardevoir’s activation, starting role or appearance against Mt. Silver. Haunter continues with two reported weeks out. Cerulean’s Watchog has a new eighteen-week designation before the Tide’s must-win game with Vermilion.
The Johto East decider and other returns

Blackthorn’s Exploud has a new two-week absence after rushing for thirty-seven yards against Mahogany. Sawsbuck remains out five weeks. Lavender’s Mr. Clanky continues at six weeks, while People Eater has reached zero remaining weeks. Moth Ball’s five-touchdown performance establishes what the available quarterback did against Violet; it does not establish the injured starter’s return.

Cinnabar’s Seismitoad has reached zero remaining weeks, while Arcanine remains out two and Octillery one. Other cleared remaining absences include Fortree’s Pawmot, Mahogany’s Jellicent, Lavaridge’s Mantine, Azalea’s Castform and Celadon’s Anorith. A countdown reaching zero differs from a recorded game appearance. The table retains both new entries and ordinary recovery changes so those developments are not conflated.

articles.title: Game of the Week: Lavender and Blackthorn play for Johto East
articles.dek: The Wails need a win. The Dragons can retain first with a win or tie. Third seed, a home opener and a trip to Cinnabar are all attached to the result.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Lavender has spent the past two weeks making its passing game look capable of deciding a division. Now it gets precisely that assignment. The Wails host Blackthorn in the final regular-season round, with a win giving Lavender the Johto East championship and any other result sending the Dragons home with the title. Both clubs have secured playoff berths. The difference is whether the postseason starts in their own stadium or somebody else’s.

My pick is Lavender 31, Blackthorn 27. Moth Ball threw five touchdown passes in the 51–10 win at Violet, and Hobbes added 116 rushing yards and two scores. Blackthorn answered its own difficult previous week with a 27–19 victory at Mahogany. Hatterene completed twenty-one of twenty-eight passes for 275 yards and two touchdowns there. These are two passing games with fresh evidence of production, meeting in a game where the standings give neither staff a reason to save its best ideas.
One result changes two playoff assignments

Blackthorn enters at 12–4, Lavender at 11–5. A Wails victory puts both clubs at twelve wins, with Lavender taking the division through the applicable tiebreak. The winner of the division occupies the conference’s third seed, while the other club finishes fifth. A tie leaves Blackthorn ahead on record, so Lavender needs to win outright. There is no useful draw for a home crowd expecting a division celebration.

The third seed hosts the sixth seed on opening weekend. The fifth seed travels to fourth-seeded Cinnabar. That is a substantial difference in preparation and travel, even before considering which opponent eventually occupies sixth. Vermilion currently holds that position, but Olivine can move ahead with a win coupled with a Volts loss. The full Playoff Race feature carries those branches; this game decides which Johto East club gets to watch them from the division winner’s chair.

Blackthorn’s one-win advantage therefore gives it two acceptable results, a win or a tie. It does not make a cautious offensive approach automatically sensible. Lavender just scored seven touchdowns at Violet. The Dragons will have to make a sequence of stops before they can treat their favorable standings position as protection. A passive first half could turn the arithmetic into something their offense has to repair under pressure.
Moth Ball has several credible destinations

Moth Ball completed twenty-one of thirty-seven passes for 300 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions against Violet. His protection allowed no sacks. The completion rate leaves room for improvement, but the combination of explosive gains, touchdown distribution and clean possessions makes that passing line especially useful before a game of this size. Lavender created separation without paying for its ambitious throws in turnovers.

Might Guy supplied the largest receiving total: four catches for 122 yards, including a forty-six-yard gain and a twenty-four-yard touchdown. Luvdisc caught eleven passes for 101 yards and two touchdowns. Those lines describe different problems for Blackthorn. One receiver can move the ball a long distance on a small number of completions; another can keep appearing often enough to sustain possessions. Assigning all the defensive attention to either one leaves a productive alternative.

The Wail added three catches for thirty yards and a fourteen-yard touchdown. Unfezant scored on a seven-yard reception. Four receivers caught touchdown passes in total. That makes the coverage assignment more demanding than containing a single spectacular player. Blackthorn needs its secondary to communicate through the full receiving group, particularly after Lavender gets close enough that a short completion can finish the drive.

The Dragons should judge their early defensive work by whether they can make Lavender finish long possessions. A single reception to Might Guy can undo several otherwise sound snaps. Keeping those gains in front of the coverage would force Moth Ball to complete more throws, and his sixteen incompletions against Violet show that the passing game does leave opportunities to end a series. The forecast depends on Blackthorn limiting damage rather than expecting the Wails to stop attempting difficult throws.
Hobbes keeps the passing plan practical

Hobbes carried eighteen times for 116 yards and two touchdowns at Violet, then added a thirty-yard reception. Lavender can ask Blackthorn to defend a productive runner while also accounting for several receiving targets. That combination supports my pick more than the five-touchdown passing total by itself. If the Dragons make the Wails spend a possession running, Lavender has a recent answer that does not require abandoning its best players.

The measurable test is whether Hobbes can again reach one hundred rushing yards without Lavender needing an unusually large number of attempts. His last performance averaged more than six yards per carry. Blackthorn does not have to hold him to nothing; it does need enough short gains to create passing situations in which the rush and coverage can anticipate the same assignment. Repeated easy rushing yards would make the explosive receiving threats harder to manage.

Mr. Clanky remains on the injury report with six weeks remaining. That continuing absence belongs in the evaluation even after Lavender’s large win. The Wails cannot assume that the same protection result will recur against a different opponent. People Eater’s remaining injury counter has reached zero, but that counter alone does not confirm a lineup assignment. Any return should be judged from actual participation, not written into the preview as an established starter change.
Hatterene can keep Blackthorn within one possession

Hatterene’s Mahogany performance gives Blackthorn a persuasive reason to remain aggressive. Twenty-one completions in twenty-eight attempts is a three-quarter completion rate, and 275 yards means those completions did more than avoid mistakes. The quarterback threw two touchdown passes. The Dragons scored twenty-seven points and won by eight, a useful response after the previous round’s heavy defeat at Saffron.

Furret caught six passes for 134 yards and a touchdown against Mahogany. Lavender has to account for that production before deciding how freely it can pressure Hatterene. A defense that commits too many resources to the passer can leave a productive receiver with the kind of space that changes a close game. The Wails need to pressure the throw while maintaining coverage responsibilities beyond the first few yards of the route.

Blackthorn’s running options carry an immediate injury complication. Exploud gained thirty-seven yards on nine carries at Mahogany and now appears with a two-week absence. Sawsbuck still has five weeks remaining. Those reports reduce the grounds for assuming that the Dragons can reproduce the same backfield distribution in the finale. A possible replacement can be discussed as a possibility; the current evidence does not establish who receives every vacated carry.

That uncertainty puts more responsibility on Hatterene’s ordinary completions. Blackthorn may need the passing game to produce the manageable second downs that a steady rushing performance would otherwise supply. Furret’s receiving work gives it an obvious route, but Lavender will enter with that same information. The Dragons’ other targets must make enough contributions that the Wails cannot devote their entire coverage plan to one receiver.
Takeaways could decide which offense gets the last useful chance

Lavender intercepted Iron Jugulis four times at Violet. Dugtrio, Octillery, Mimikyu and Noctowl each made one of those plays. Those takeaways helped the Wails separate rapidly, while Muk added a safety. Blackthorn should prepare for an active defense, but four interceptions against one quarterback are not a forecast of four against the next. Hatterene’s decisions will determine how much of that opportunity exists again.

My first benchmark is a clean turnover column for Moth Ball. The Wails can win a close game through their passing range and Hobbes’s production, but a giveaway would hand Blackthorn a shorter route to the points it needs. My second is holding Furret below another hundred-yard receiving afternoon. Lavender can survive individual Blackthorn gains; repeatedly allowing its leading receiver to move entire possessions would make a thirty-one-point winning total harder to defend.

The expected game is closer than Lavender’s last result because Blackthorn brings a productive quarterback and an immediate championship incentive. I favor the home team’s combination of rushing and receiving options, especially after seeing Moth Ball distribute five touchdown throws without an interception. Lavender 31, Blackthorn 27 gives the Wails the third seed and a home playoff opener, while sending the Dragons to Cinnabar. Blackthorn can reverse that forecast by protecting its possessions and forcing Lavender to complete more plays before each score.

body.text: Twelve playoff places are secured. Two remain, one in each conference, and Johto East is the only undecided division. Mt. Silver joins Mossdeep with a confirmed first seed and bye. Petalburg and Eterna have secured their divisions, while Dewford, Rustboro and Vermilion have secured berths. The final regular-season round will decide the remaining entrants and several first-round matchups.

Blackthorn at Lavender is the clearest division game: a Wails win gives Lavender the title and third seed; a Dragons win or tie gives Blackthorn both. The other club finishes fifth and visits fourth-seeded Cinnabar in the wild-card round. Both teams have already qualified. That distinction separates a home-game opportunity from a win-or-go-home qualification game.

body.text: Kanto–Johto: follow Olivine, then Violet

Olivine visits Azalea. A win puts the Ironclads in regardless of every other result. If Vermilion loses at Cerulean in that case, Olivine takes sixth and Vermilion seventh; otherwise Vermilion is sixth and Olivine seventh. A tie at Azalea is enough for Olivine only if Violet fails to beat Mahogany. A Violet win then takes the last berth.

If Olivine loses, a Violet win or tie takes the final berth. If both Olivine and Violet lose, Cerulean takes it by beating Vermilion. If Cerulean also fails to win, Cianwood takes it by winning at Mt. Silver. If none of those clubs supplies the needed result, Olivine survives at 8–9. Cerulean’s winning route does not require Cianwood to lose; the Tide wins the relevant eight-win comparison.

body.text: The matchups make some routes harder than their short descriptions suggest. Olivine must improve on three points against Cianwood while replacing Gogoat, now out five reported weeks. Violet must recover from a four-interception loss without Zangoose, out four. Cerulean needs a victory over a nine-win opponent and two specific losses elsewhere. Cianwood must win at the conference’s top seed, then receive the necessary help. None of these routes is a probability estimate.
Hoenn–Sinnoh: Mauville has the first move

Mauville qualifies with a win at Petalburg. If the Dynamos fail to win, a Canalave win at Oreburgh gives the Bulwark the final berth. If neither wins, a Hearthome win over Pastoria gives the Haunts the place. Those three first checks settle every combination containing a win by one of the contenders.

If none wins, the tie branches decide it. A Mauville tie earns the berth. If Mauville loses, a Canalave tie earns it. If both Mauville and Canalave lose, a Hearthome tie earns it. If all three lose, Mauville survives. This ordering includes Hearthome’s existing tie and the native tiebreak results; simply comparing the number of wins would miss several of these outcomes.

body.text: Dewford at Rustboro determines fifth and sixth in Hoenn–Sinnoh. A Stone win gives Rustboro fifth and Dewford sixth. A Dewford win or a tie keeps the Breakers fifth and the Stone sixth. Both are already qualified, so the game changes their likely first-round opponent rather than whether they have a postseason.

Sunyshore secures second with a win or tie at Veilstone, and also remains second if Petalburg fails to win. If Petalburg wins and Sunyshore loses, both finish 12–5 and strength of victory decides their order, with strength of schedule resolving an exact tie. The five-game check below covers every remaining combination. Petalburg finishes fourth if it loses and Eterna wins; otherwise it is third unless that five-game check moves it to second.

Only if Sunyshore loses and Petalburg wins: add one point for each victory and half a point for each tie by Cinnabar, Mahogany, Rustboro, Snowpoint and Hearthome. Three or more points keeps Sunyshore second and Petalburg third. Two and a half or fewer puts Petalburg second and Sunyshore third. These points summarize the strength-of-victory comparison; they are not predicted scores or playoff odds.
The bracket that follows

The first seed in each conference rests. The second seed hosts seventh, third hosts sixth, and fourth hosts fifth. The divisional round reseeds: the highest remaining seed hosts the lowest remaining seed. That means a lower seed cannot be assigned a fixed second-round opponent before the wild-card games are played.

Kanto–Johto has unusually clear anchors: Mt. Silver first, Saffron second and Cinnabar fourth. The Johto East decider fills third and fifth; Vermilion and the final qualifier fill sixth and seventh. Saffron will host seventh. Cinnabar will host whichever of Blackthorn and Lavender does not take the division. The division winner will host sixth.

In Hoenn–Sinnoh, Mossdeep waits through the wild-card round. Sunyshore, Petalburg and Eterna fill the other division-winner positions. Dewford and Rustboro fill fifth and sixth, with their final head-to-head result deciding the order; Mauville, Canalave or Hearthome takes seventh. The charts identify every remaining berth route, while the unplayed seeding comparisons remain conditional.

The route calculations use recorded results and the league’s native tiebreak procedures. Every berth branch settles before strength of victory. The Sunyshore–Petalburg comparison was checked separately: strength of victory can favor either club, while Petalburg has the stronger schedule in every remaining combination. Future scores are not used to award a point-based tiebreak.

body.text: The final regular-season slate has one direct division decider, two final wild-card places and an unbeaten team chasing its seventeenth victory. Blackthorn at Lavender is the Game of the Week. Dewford at Rustboro settles fifth and sixth in Hoenn–Sinnoh, while Mauville, Canalave and Hearthome pursue the final berth through separate games. Every matchup and all eighty writer forecasts appear below.

I went 12–4 last week. Mara Voss went 15–1 and chose Petalburg while I favored Rustboro 27–20. The Pride won 17–10, with two Flygon interceptions and only one Stone touchdown. Rustboro’s passing yardage did not become the balanced scoring I expected. That is the correction I carry into this week’s Dewford forecast: productive gains need a credible route to finished possessions.

My Mossdeep forecast also gave the offense too much credit: I expected 41–10, and the Eclipse won 22–3 with Budew Baker starting. The defense still provided a strong foundation, but the current available lineup matters when projecting the points. Poury Holt’s new absence is part of this week’s assessment. No unannounced resting plan is assumed for a club with a secured seed.

The targets below are checkable matchup goals. The scores are each writer’s independent judgment, including large mismatches, close games and one predicted tie. They are not playoff probabilities. The separate playoff feature gives the exact qualification consequences of wins, losses and ties.

matchups.matchup: Two five-win teams get a direct final comparison
matchups.analysis: Celadon lost 24–7 to Cinnabar; Viridian lost 20–13 to Pewter despite winning the turnover count. Both offenses need to finish more possessions. I favor Viridian’s recent ball security in a close game, with neither team having earned a large scoring projection.

matchups.homeKey: Allow no more than one touchdown pass.

matchups.matchup: Cinnabar brings a productive passing game to a six-win defense
matchups.analysis: Glalie caught twelve passes for 154 yards and two touchdowns at Celadon. Pewter recovered to beat Viridian but surrendered three possessions. Cinnabar’s fourth seed is fixed; the recent receiving production still supplies the stronger forecast.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least sixty percent of passes.
matchups.homeKey: Lose no more than one turnover.

matchups.matchup: Vermilion’s seed meets Cerulean’s last route
matchups.analysis: The Volts have qualified; the Tide must win and have both Olivine and Violet lose. Farigiraf threw two touchdowns against Saffron without an interception, but Cerulean converted only one third down. Vermilion’s 17–14 win offers a narrow scoring advantage, not a comfortable one.
matchups.awayKey: Produce at least three scoring possessions.
matchups.homeKey: Convert at least forty percent of third downs.

matchups.matchup: Saffron prepares from a fixed second seed
matchups.analysis: The Psi Corps have allowed 128 points through sixteen games and just scored four touchdowns at Cerulean. Fuchsia lost 17–14 to Vermilion. The Shadows need an unusually clean offensive game to stay close to a team producing both rushing and passing scores.
matchups.awayKey: Throw no interceptions and convert four third downs.
matchups.homeKey: Allow no more than fourteen points.

matchups.matchup: Olivine can settle the wild-card race itself
matchups.analysis: A win puts the Ironclads in. They must replace Gogoat after scoring three points at Cianwood, while Azalea went zero for eleven on third down against Mt. Silver. Bibarel’s zero remaining injury weeks is useful availability information, though it does not announce his role.
matchups.awayKey: Score at least two offensive touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Convert at least three third downs.

matchups.matchup: Cianwood’s playoff route begins at the top seed
matchups.analysis: The Crushers remain alive after a 10–3 win built on Bibarel’s carries and late takeaways. Mt. Silver has the bye secured and is adjusting to Tony Gyarzalez’s absence. Gardevoir has zero remaining injury weeks, but Cianwood’s starting quarterback assignment is not confirmed.
matchups.awayKey: Avoid interceptions and exceed one hundred rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Convert at least half of third downs.

matchups.matchup: Violet needs a recovery and an Olivine slip
matchups.analysis: The Falcons have a win route and a tie route, both requiring help from Olivine. Mahogany stayed within eight of Blackthorn. Violet must reduce the four interceptions from its Lavender loss while replacing Zangoose’s rushing work.
matchups.homeKey: Throw no more than one interception.

matchups.matchup: Johto East will be decided here
matchups.analysis: Lavender takes the division with a win; Blackthorn takes it with a win or tie. Moth Ball threw five touchdowns against Violet, while Hatterene answered Blackthorn’s previous collapse with 275 yards at Mahogany. Exploud’s two-week absence complicates the Dragons’ balance.
matchups.awayKey: Score three touchdowns and lose no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Pressure Hatterene without allowing two thirty-yard completions.

matchups.matchup: Two confirmed wild cards decide fifth and sixth
matchups.analysis: Rustboro takes fifth with a win; a tie or Dewford victory keeps the Breakers there. Both teams won useful defensive downs last week, but Rustboro lost two passes to Flygon. Dewford’s kickoff touchdown helped compensate for only 194 offensive yards.
matchups.awayKey: Convert at least four third downs.
matchups.homeKey: Lose no more than one possession to turnovers.

matchups.matchup: Mauville’s win-and-in game meets a changed Pride backfield
matchups.analysis: The Dynamos qualify with a win. Petalburg has secured Hoenn West but lost Oinkologne for three weeks after his 119 scrimmage yards at Rustboro. Togekiss produced 247 passing yards at Dewford; Mauville needs that production to become sustained scoring.
matchups.awayKey: Convert at least three third downs.

matchups.analysis: The Eclipse remain unbeaten after Budew Baker’s winning start, but Poury Holt is now out seven weeks. Lavaridge has won three straight and is eliminated from the playoffs. The finale tests Mossdeep’s available offense against a club that can still spoil a perfect regular season.
matchups.awayKey: Allow no more than two sacks and one turnover.

matchups.matchup: Two eliminated division rivals finish the schedule
matchups.analysis: Sootopolis allowed seven sacks at Mossdeep, while Fortree scored three at Lavaridge. The Surge have the better record and a useful Pawmo receiving contribution to build on, but both offenses need to show they can sustain ordinary possessions.
matchups.awayKey: Allow no more than three sacks.

matchups.matchup: Canalave’s final chance comes with new absences
matchups.analysis: The Bulwark must beat Oreburgh and have Mauville fail to win for a guaranteed berth. Nidoking and Seismitoad are newly unavailable. Slowking threw three touchdowns against Snowpoint; Oreburgh’s defense just held Eterna to fifteen.
matchups.awayKey: Throw no interceptions and score two touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Canalave below one hundred rushing yards.

matchups.analysis: The Thorns have secured Sinnoh West, but their quarterback has a seven-week injury designation and Stantler two. Snowpoint scored twenty-one at Canalave. Eterna’s defense has allowed 181 points all season; the available offense is the largest uncertainty in this matchup.
matchups.awayKey: Avoid interceptions and reach twenty points.

matchups.matchup: Hearthome needs its result and two others
matchups.analysis: The Haunts qualify with a win if both Mauville and Canalave fail to win; a tie works if both lose. Pastoria was held to 111 yards by Sunyshore. Feraligatr’s ninety-seven rushing yards give Hearthome the more dependable recent offensive contribution.
matchups.awayKey: Convert at least three third downs.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for at least ninety yards.

matchups.matchup: Sunyshore can secure second with a road win
matchups.analysis: The Starseekers recovered with 305 passing yards and three touchdowns at Pastoria. Veilstone lost 21–7 to Hearthome and has a new Kricketune absence. A Sunyshore win locks down second seed; the passing matchups favor that outcome.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least sixty percent of passes.
matchups.homeKey: Allow no more than two passing touchdowns.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Viridian collected three takeaways and still lost. I expect the defense to give the Titans another chance, and the offense to use enough of it.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Celadon managed four third-down conversions against Cinnabar. I trust that capacity to sustain a few drives against a less imposing opponent.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Both clubs have five wins and recent trouble finishing possessions. Their available evidence supports a low-scoring tie as my best single score judgment.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Viridian’s passing game avoided interceptions against Pewter. Celadon just spent a full afternoon failing to answer Cinnabar’s scoring, and I expect another limited output.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Titans’ clean passing turnover line and useful Gabite carries give them a small advantage if they defend the final possession better.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cinnabar has beaten Blackthorn, Mt. Silver and Celadon in succession. Pewter’s comeback was admirable; the three giveaways make another recovery much harder here.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Gholdengo took no sacks on thirty-five attempts. That protection should let Cinnabar keep testing a defense that could not turn Viridian’s low output into an easy win.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Pewter showed a late response rather than folding at Viridian. I still favor Cinnabar’s repeated receiving production, but give the home side two touchdowns.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Blaine has Glalie catching everything useful and Gholdengo distributing without sack losses. Pewter’s three-turnover afternoon is a dreadful preparation for that assignment.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Blaze’s passing efficiency and better recent opponents favor another win. Pewter needs a much cleaner possession count than it supplied last week.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cerulean completed useful passes against Saffron and avoided interceptions. I think that offense can beat a Vermilion team whose nine wins have required considerable restraint from its scoring.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Tide ran only six times and converted one of five third downs. Vermilion can keep the game short enough for its defense to decide it.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Cerulean’s passing line was better than its final margin against Saffron. I expect the home offense to find more repeatable gains against the Volts.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Vermilion has just finished a close game successfully. Cerulean needs several things to go right and has not shown enough sustained offense to make its own part likely.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Volts’ recent seventeen-point win and secured berth support a modest edge. Cerulean can threaten through the air but must improve its possession length.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Saffron followed seventy points with four more touchdowns and no turnovers. Fuchsia’s three-win offense offers little evidence that it can disrupt that control.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Skattebo’s short scoring runs give Saffron an answer beyond its receivers. Fuchsia will have to defend the full possession, and I do not expect it to do so repeatedly.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Fuchsia kept Vermilion within three points. Saffron is substantially stronger, but a final-round game can still contain several ordinary scoring interruptions for the favorite.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Psi Corps have conceded eight points a game across sixteen weeks. Fuchsia’s recent fourteen against Vermilion does not persuade me it reaches the end zone here.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Saffron’s combination of efficient passing, short-yardage finishing and strong defense supports a large margin against an opponent with three wins.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Azalea could not convert a third down even with two takeaways helping. Olivine’s offense is limited, but this opponent gives it a workable route to the berth.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Ironclads allowed only ten points to Cianwood. Their defense can keep the game within reach while the offense works around Gogoat’s absence.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Olivine’s new backfield absence follows a three-point performance. Azalea’s kicking supplied all nine points last week; one touchdown alongside it could change this result.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Swarm’s offense turned eleven third downs into eleven failures. Olivine does not need brilliance to win this particular final examination.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Olivine’s passing completion rate was respectable despite its poor total. Against an Azalea offense struggling to extend drives, a modest improvement should be sufficient.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Mt. Silver produced 453 yards and never punted at Azalea. Cianwood’s three-completion win gives the Reds a substantial offensive advantage even with a receiving absence.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Gurdurr’s late takeaways and Cianwood’s five sacks show a defense capable of resistance. I still favor the Reds’ protection and more dependable passing.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Crushers have earned a meaningful finale through defense and Bibarel’s persistence. Mt. Silver remains the better team, though the new receiving injuries make a smaller margin sensible.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Crem Ftzpatrik has just thrown three touchdowns without taking a sack. Cianwood will need far more than three completions to answer the Reds at home.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mt. Silver’s passing distribution and rushing support should create more sustained offense. Cianwood’s quarterback availability improves, but its actual lineup and passing recovery remain uncertain.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Mahogany stayed competitive with Blackthorn while Violet gave away four passes. The Falcons’ new rushing absence makes an immediate offensive repair less convincing.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Violet’s worst damage came from passing mistakes and short opportunities. I expect a more conservative game against Mahogany to preserve enough scoring chances.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Falcons still have a concrete route and a home game. Mahogany can make it difficult, but Violet has enough recent wins before the collapse to earn a narrow recovery pick.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Four interceptions and a lost Zangoose contribution are a poor foundation for a must-improve afternoon. Mahogany’s nineteen against Blackthorn is the stronger recent scoring evidence.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Violet should face less passing pressure from the scoreboard than it did against Lavender. I expect fewer risky throws and enough touchdowns to keep its playoff route alive.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Lavender’s five passing touchdowns came without a sack or interception. Blackthorn recovered at Mahogany, but its recent defensive volatility makes me favor the Wails at home.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Wails can pressure a Blackthorn offense missing two backs while giving Moth Ball multiple receiving outlets. That combination should produce a clearer margin than the records alone suggest.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Lavender has kept winning through its quarterback absence and now gets the division opportunity at home. Hatterene’s recovery makes me expect a game decided by one late possession.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Hatterene completed twenty-one of twenty-eight at Mahogany. I trust that sharper passing to test Lavender more effectively than Violet’s four-interception offense did.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Moth Ball’s protection and Luvdisc’s repeated availability give Lavender a slight scoring edge. Blackthorn can answer through Hatterene, but its backfield absences reduce the margin for stalled drives.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Dewford stopped all eight Mauville third downs. Rustboro’s two interceptions and sixty-eight rushing yards leave the Breakers with a plausible route to another narrow defensive win.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: I trust Dewford’s protection after zero sacks allowed more than Rustboro’s reliance on one receiver for most of its passing yards. The Breakers can make the Stone repeat difficult downs.

picks.author: ellis-quill

picks.author: dorian-pike

picks.author: tessa-wren

picks.author: rowan-vale

picks.author: mara-voss

picks.author: ellis-quill

picks.author: tessa-wren

picks.author: tessa-wren

picks.reason: Feraligatr supplied ninety-seven yards while the defense held Veilstone to seven. I expect that balance to create repeated difficult passing downs for the Waves.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Hearthome has kept its season relevant through useful late results. Pastoria can respond after a poor game, but the Haunts have the steadier current contributions.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Haunts remain below .500 and should not receive an effortless victory in the forecast. Pastoria’s offense was poor, yet a modest recovery can keep this within one possession.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Hearthome’s running game and recent defensive result provide the better foundation. Pastoria must improve both protection and third downs before I expect enough points to win.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Watzon found three touchdown throws without an interception at Pastoria. Veilstone’s seven-point response at Hearthome does not suggest it can match that production.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Sunyshore held Pastoria to one conversion in nine third downs. The Fists’ recent offensive struggles give the Starseekers a similar route to sustained defensive control.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The visitors have earned twelve wins and just repaired their passing game. I expect Veilstone to offer some home resistance while Sunyshore’s stronger balance decides it.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: I still want to see Sunyshore repeat this against a leading defense. Veilstone’s current scoring and Kricketune absence make this a much easier assignment.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Starseekers have multiple receivers producing useful yardage and a defense that just forced eight punts. Veilstone’s limited recent offense leaves a clear gap.
